title: borealis-retail-integration-call-notes-2026-04-20
content:
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood CS), Ethan Li (Redwood Solutions), Priya Singh (Redwood AM), Laura Kim (Borealis PM), Daniel Ortiz (Borealis Engineering), Sara Müller (Borealis Ops)

Meeting objective: kick-off integration + surface requirements, constraints, and immediate follow-ups for Borealis Retail Proof-of-Concept (PoC). They want in-store assistant + post-purchase support (chat + embeddings for KB).

High-level summary:
- Borealis is running a pilot in 30 stores starting July. Primary goals: quick answers to POS staff, reduce escalations to support, and power a knowledge base for returns + promotions.
- Pilot traffic estimate: 5k queries/day per store peak? (they gave rough numbers; Daniel to confirm). Expected concurrency patterns: short bursts at opening/closing and during promotions.
- Data sensitivity: customer PII in receipts; they want options for on-prem/private deployment for regulatory reasons but are open to Redwood Dedicated for pilot if we provide clear data flows and SOC2 artefacts.

Tech requirements / constraints:
- Latency SLO: 300–500ms p95 for short chat queries (<=100 tokens). They emphasized customer experience - store staff must not wait.
- Throughput: pilot baseline ~150k tokens/day but could spike; need autoscaling/burst plan.
- Embeddings: KB ~120k docs (short paragraphs), want embed + semantic search + reranking.
- Model preferences: prefer open weights. Laura asked about recommended model tradeoffs: Ethan suggested redwood-rt-large-1 quantized with Dedicated for cost/latency balance; fallback to hosted smaller model for heavy load.
- Security: require KMS integration, audit logs retention 1 year, and option for traffic to stay in their VPC for private deployment later.

Gotchas / risks called out by Borealis:
- POS environment has flaky NAT + occasional outbound IP changes; they insisted on resilient client SDKs and connection backoff strategies.
- They process PII in receipts; legal will likely push for Private deployment for production. Need to surface compliance checklist early.
- Volume estimates are uncertain — they under/over-provision in internal metrics; recommend conservative capacity with auto-burst credits during promotions.

Open questions (action owners in parens):
- Confirm expected queries/day and token distribution per query (Daniel) — due 2026-04-24. (Daniel)
- Which KB export format will Borealis provide? (CSV, JSONL, or direct DB export). They said "CSV first" but will confirm. (Laura)
- Billing and pricing model for pilot (usage vs Dedicated): provide cost scenarios based on 3 model choices + quantization options (Ethan) — deliver 2026-04-23.
- Legal/Compliance: what specific controls do they need for PII? ask for their checklist. (Priya)

Immediate next steps / TODOs:
- Redwood: send onboarding checklist + proposed architecture diagram for Dedicated + Private options (Maya) — by 2026-04-22.
- Solutions Eng (Ethan): produce 3 cost/perf scenarios (hosted small, dedicated quantized large, private on-prem) with rough monthly costs and latency estimates (2026-04-23).
- Customer: share KB sample (50–100 rows) and traffic stats (Daniel) — target 2026-04-24.
- Schedule technical deep-dive with Borealis eng team (include SRE + infra) week of 2026-04-27. (Maya/Ethan)

Notes for internal follow-up (notes to self):
- Consider recommending prefix KV caching and aggressive batching policies for embeddings ingestion. Might need offline ingestion pipeline + deduping.
- For POS NAT issues: propose SDK with retry/backoff and local queueing; possibly edge proxy option. Flag to infra team.
- Prepare a short one-pager comparing Dedicated vs Private for compliance customers — highlight differences in network control, audit logs, and cost. (Priya)

Potential blockers:
- Legal holdouts on PII could push timeline; start collecting our SOC2/KMS docs now.
- If traffic is much higher than estimates, pilot may require Dedicated from day 1 — need quick contract path.

Customer quotes / tone:
- Laura: "We need it to feel instantaneous — the staff can't wait for model heats."
- Daniel: "We want a path to keep data inside our network eventually."

Misc scribbles / brainstorming:
- Can we offer a short-term hybrid: Dedicated serving with private network peering + masking of PII at ingestion?
- Evaluate embedding compression options to reduce storage for 120k docs.

Action owner list (condensed):
- Maya: onboarding checklist + diagrams (2026-04-22)
- Ethan: cost scenarios + model recommendations (2026-04-23)
- Priya: legal/compliance ask + SOC2/KMS links (2026-04-22)
- Daniel/Laura: KB sample + traffic confirmation (2026-04-24)

End of notes.

Internal status: still early-stage - these are working notes. Will convert to a one-pager for AE handoff once we have KB sample and traffic numbers.
